rule: Take the first panel, which holds one mirror-symmetric shape with a unique tip plus single dots. From the tip, the shape moves to the nearest dot straight ahead, or else turns left/right to the nearest in-line dot and rotates to face it. It is re-stamped with its tip on the dot, which is eaten. This repeats until no dot is ahead or to either side. Output one panel showing only the shape at its final position and orientation.
scope: Infer an arrow's tip, follow nearest dots with forward priority and left/right turns, then predict the final shape from one or more animation snapshots. Random panel height 7..30 and width bounded by total input width 30; one to four default panels, up to six requested; random symmetric connected arrows and controlled 2..20-eat paths.

authored_scope: Supported: 1-6 panels (default 1-4), with later panels being consistent intermediate snapshots. Panel height 3-30 (default 7-18) and width 3-30 (default 6-18), with total width <= 30. Sizes beyond the fixture range of 8-15 are synthetic extensions. Random distinct bg/divider/shape colours. Random connected symmetric arrow shapes (depth 1-3, half-width <= 2) with exactly one qualifying tip direction. Walks of 2-12 eats mixing straight runs and turns. Optional explicit control of tip, direction, shape, size, panel count and snapshots. Deliberately not supported: uneaten leftover dots, left/right turn ties, dots adjacent to each other or to any displayed shape, non-uniform panel widths, horizontal dividers.
authored_constraints: Exactly one 8-connected multi-cell shape per panel; every dot is an isolated single cell with no 8-neighbour of shape colour
The shape has exactly one direction whose extreme cell is unique and lies on a mirror axis
The walk computed by the rule eats every dot in the given order (checked by a local re-simulation of the latent path, not the reference solver)
When a turn is required, exactly one side has an in-line dot or the two distances differ
Snapshot panels show the shape at path[k-1] facing its arrival direction, with dots path[k:]. No snapshot shape touches a remaining dot
Each stamped shape position fits inside the panel
Divider colour differs from background and shape colour; background differs from shape colour
